articles.headlineJa: NFL第9週の到着シーン：ビルスのTEダルトン・キンケイドがセイバーズへ支持を表明
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日の到着シーンを毎週のファッションショーへと変え続けている。
articles.body:
November football doesn't come with one dress code.

The South could see two takes on fall fashion on Sunday. With sunshine and temperatures in the mid-60s in Charlotte, a varsity jacket or a knit polo would fit right in. In Miami Gardens, temperatures in the 80s leave room for breezy button-downs, relaxed trousers and shades.

Out West, sunshine in Southern California and the Bay Area sets the stage for short sleeves and lighter fabrics. Seattle could call for a different approach, with possible showers in the forecast.

The Northeast and Midwest offer more chances to break out fall staples. Temperatures in the 50s in Philadelphia and Foxborough are good territory for knitwear, and a cool Sunday night in Chicago gives players a reason to pull out a statement coat for the walk into Soldier Field.

Here are the NFL's most fashionable arrivals from Week 9.

 Sunday's best

Dalton Kincaid kept it local with the Buffalo Sabres' Hometown Remix jersey, which the NHL team debuted Wednesday. The Buffalo Bills  tight end layered the blue, gold and white jersey over a gray hoodie, pairing it with dark jeans, white sneakers and a black cap. A brown leather duffel completed the look.

Detroit Lions players arrived with tributes to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell as he recovers from a neck injury. Aidan Hutchinson added a personal touch to his signature gallon water jug, labeling it "Jack," while Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, Joe Bachie, Amen Ogbongbemiga, K.J. Britt and Trevor Nowaske wore Campbell's jersey.

Campbell, who has been placed on injured reserve, said in a statement Wednesday that he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body.

Thursday night's fits

Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence doubled up on dark denim for "Thursday Night Football," pairing a zip-front jacket with matching jeans and cream sneakers. Ravens rookie linebacker Ethan Burke, who was born in Annapolis, Maryland, and grew up in nearby Pasadena, showed some love to the Washington Capitals by layering a throwback Alex Ovechkin jersey featuring the Screaming Eagle logo over a black hoodie.

articles.headline: Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, CB Riley Moss suffer concussions against Panthers
articles.description: Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss both suffered concussions against the Panthers.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコスのWRジェイレン・ワドルとCBライリー・モス、パンサーズ戦で脳震盪
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスのワイドレシーバー、ジェイレン・ワドルとコーナーバックのライリー・モスの両名が、パンサーズ戦で脳震盪を起こした。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers with a concussion as cornerback Riley Moss sustained a concussion just minutes later.

The Broncos went into the game without either of their starting safeties as Brandon Jones (hamstring) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both game-day inactives.

Second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron played in Moss' spot. Moss was injured as he made a tackle on Trevor Etienne in the second quarter.

Waddle, who had one catch Sunday for 22 yards, left the game with seconds to go in the first quarter. He reached to make a catch in front of Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson and was hit by Zakee Wheatley, who knocked the ball free.

Waddle, who has battled ankle and chest injuries already this season, jumped up after the play and walked toward the Broncos huddle but then left the field and did not return. He has 30 receptions for 337 yards and two touchdowns this season.

The Broncos (6-2) entered the day with a slim lead in the AFC West race over the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2).

articles.headline: Man United's poor starts have Premier League relegation looking more likely
articles.description: Man United have a penchant for waking up *after* games have already started -- and it's why they face Premier League relegation.
articles.headlineJa: マン・ユナイテッドの悪い立ち上がりが、プレミアリーグ降格の現実味を増させている
articles.descriptionJa: マン・ユナイテッドには、試合が始まってからようやくエンジンがかかるという癖があり、それがプレミアリーグ降格の危機に直面している理由だ。
articles.body:
Manchester United are locked in a battle to avoid relegation from the Premier League despite a dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that left England's biggest club in the bottom three and manager Michael Carrick facing the sack.

United twice overturned a two-goal deficit to salvage a point, but the result extended United's winless league run to eight games -- their worst-ever stretch in Premier League history -- and without a league win since August.

But two goals in stoppage time by substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu denied Villa the win and ensured United avoided going into the international break on the back of three straight league defeats.

Yet with United's games descending into chaos due to bad starts and late fightbacks, Carrick's failure to bring calmness and stability -- and results -- make him extremely vulnerable in his job. -- Mark Ogden

Man United face relegation because they keep putting themselves in a hole straight away

Whoever is the United manager when they next play Liverpool at Anfield later this month, the first challenge will be to stop the hugely damaging habit of starting games terribly because they face relegation if they don't.

United are falling behind before games really get going, and then they wake up late and force themselves to play catchup. United have conceded first in 10 of 15 games this season in all competitions; three of those 10 instances were in the first 10 minutes.

And guess what? It happened again against Villa with Unai Emery's side 2-0 up inside five minutes at Old Trafford. (Roma also raced into a 2-0 halftime lead in the Champions League in midweek before United pulled off an incredible fightback to win 3-2.)

No team can expect to prosper if they start games so badly on such a regular basis.

To make matters worse, United started the second half by conceding another two quick goals, making United the first team in Europe's Big Five leagues to concede 30 goals this season in all competitions.

United are the first team to concede two goals in the first 10 minutes of each half this season in the Premier League and they are the second team in Premier League history to concede two goals in the first 10 minutes of each half, and first in the last 30 seasons to do so. The only other instance was Manchester City in October 1995 against Liverpool in a 6-0 win by Liverpool.

So if United don't sort it out, they will be in a relegation battle and they might not get out of it. -- Ogden

Carrick out of his depth, and likely out of United job

Michael Carrick has surely come to the end of the road as United manager after less than 12 months in charge.

Snatching a point following another late fightback is a positive, but United were so bad for so long in this game that the manager must answer questions about how his team can be so easy to score against.

Manchester United are the first team in Europe's Big Five Leagues to concede 30 goals this season in all competitions.

articles.headline: Leeds condemn 'disgusting' alleged racist abuse of Jayden Bogle after Spurs game
articles.description: Leeds have condemned alleged racist abuse of defender Jayden Bogle on social media following Saturday's 1-0 Premier League win over Tottenham at Elland Road.
articles.headlineJa: リーズ、スパーズ戦後のジェイデン・ボーグルに対する「不快な」人種差別的暴言疑惑を非難
articles.descriptionJa: エランド・ロードで行われた土曜日のプレミアリーグ、トッテナム戦での1-0の勝利後、ディフェンダーのジェイデン・ボーグルに対するSNS上での人種差別的暴言の疑惑に対し、リーズは非難の声明を出した。
articles.body:
Leeds have condemned alleged racist abuse of defender Jayden Bogle on social media following Saturday's 1-0 Premier League win over Tottenham at Elland Road.

Bogle escaped a red or yellow card after catching Spurs forward Mathys Tel on the Achilles with his studs in a first-half challenge.

The Leeds wing-back was not punished by on-field referee John Brooks and, after a lengthy VAR deliberation, it was concluded there had been no serious foul play.

A Leeds statement on Sunday read: "Leeds United Football Club are appalled at the disgusting, racist social media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered following Saturday's Premier League victory against Tottenham Hotspur.

"Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

"The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

"Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his teammates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse."

Tottenham said they were "disgusted" to hear of the abuse.

"We have offered Leeds United our support in identifying those responsible and we will pursue every available avenue to ensure they are identified and face the full consequences of their actions," Spurs said in a statement.

The Premier League added on X: "Anybody found guilty of committing discriminatory abuse will face club bans and criminal prosecution."

Tel received extensive treatment after Bogle's challenge and was later replaced by Dominic Solanke.

The Press Association understands the north London club will write to Pro Ref to seek clarification over why Bogle was not shown a red card.

In his post-match news conference, Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi did not directly comment on whether he felt Bogle should have been sent off.

But the Italian questioned Brooks' decision-making throughout the game and said the club were waiting to learn the full extent of Tel's injury.

articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 9 Buzz 

Week 9 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 9

Biggest concerns ahead of Sunday

Falcons, Bengals players in Spain

No injuries of note
Players with early starts

ACTIVE

 Harold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns (groin): Fannin was added to the injury report Thursday, before being removed Friday. He is active in Week 9. He is a strong play in fantasy this week. It's a favorable matchup against the Saints for Fannin, who averaged 14.6 fantasy PPG with Sanders last year (9.9 with other QBs) and is coming off two huge performances.

 Jake Ferguson, TE, Cowboys (ankle): Ferguson is active after exiting early last week and missing practice to start the week. With Pickens out, Ferguson could operate as the number two target for Prescott. That has him as a low-end TE1. Some tight ends to play him over are Dallas Goedert, Dalton Kincaid and Juwan Johnson.

  Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR, Lions (ribs): St. Brown has been limited at practice this week but is active for Week 9. He is a must-start fantasy option.

 Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (knee): Nabers is active in Week 9. He is a must-start in fantasy football.

 Breece Hall, RB, Jets (quad): Hall will play in Week 9. Braelon Allen has played great in Hall's absence, so expect him to have a larger role than he did previously. But Hall is still the Jets' RB1. The Chiefs are a tough matchup, so fantasy managers should temper expectations, but Hall is still in play as an RB2. As for Allen, managers should certainly hold him as he is one of the best backup RBs in the NFL. It's also possible that he has a large enough role to have stand-alone flex value.

 Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (hamstring): The Saints' first-round pick practiced in a limited fashion this week and will make his NFL debut in Week 9. While it is exciting to have Tyson back, fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Not only is it his first regular-season NFL game, but the Browns are a tough defense. Tyson returning makes it difficult to trust Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

 Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles (hamstring/back): Barkley returned to the practice field Thursday and is officially active Week 9. While he has been toughing it out through these injuries, it has led to him seeing limited usage. His big-play potential and touchdown upside keep him in the RB2 range. Some backs I would play over him are Jonah Coleman, Ollie Gordon II, Josh Jacobs, Ashton Jeanty and Quinshon Judkins.

articles.headline: Thunder get Nique Clifford in trade with Kings, sources say
articles.description: The Thunder have acquired 2025 first-round pick Nique Clifford in a trade with the Kings, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: サンダース、キングスとのトレードでニーク・クリフォードを獲得（関係者談）
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのシャムス・チャラニア氏が伝えたところによると、サンダースはキングスとのトレードにより、2025年ドラフト1巡目指名権のニーク・クリフォードを獲得した。
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings are trading second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder for two second-round picks, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Sunday.

In return, the Kings will receive a 2028 Utah Jazz second-rounder and a 2030 Minnesota Timberwolves second-rounder out of the Thunder's deep asset cupboard, sources said.

The Kings initially acquired Clifford in the 2025 draft, trading a top-16-protected 2027 San Antonio Spurs first-round pick to the Thunder to move up to the No. 24 pick and grab Clifford. It was the first move of general manager Scott Perry's tenure.

But Clifford never caught on in Sacramento and has recently been buried in coach Doug Christie's rotation despite injuries ahead of him, leading both sides -- the Kings' and Clifford's -- to seek a new home for the 24-year-old.

The Thunder are in need on the wing after a rash of early-season injuries. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, both starters, are out for several months and perhaps the entire season. Wallace tore the labrum in his left shoulder and Williams fractured his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle in the same late October home game against the LA Clippers.

That led the Thunder to go searching for help, landing on Clifford, who is making only $3.2 million this season and $3.4 million next season. The Kings, in return, get a pair of draft assets and clear a roster spot as they search for any type of success in a 1-8 start to the season. The Thunder, despite the injuries, are 8-2.

articles.headline: Roy Keane likens Michael Carrick to 'politician' after chaotic Man United draw
articles.description: "Manchester United legend Roy Keane has compared under-pressure manager Michael Carrick to a "politician," accusing him of talking a lot but saying little as his side's struggles continue.
articles.headlineJa: マンUの混乱した引き分け後、ロイ・キーンがマイケル・キャリックを「政治家」に例える
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのレジェンド、ロイ・キーンは、プレッシャーにさらされているマイケル・キャリック監督を「政治家」に例え、チームの苦境が続く中で「口先ばかりで肝心なことは何も語っていない」と批判した。
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Roy Keane has compared under-pressure manager Michael Carrick to a "politician," accusing him of talking a lot but saying little as his side's struggles continue.

In a dramatic game against Aston Villa on Sunday, United fell two goals behind inside four minutes before fighting back to level by half-time, only to concede twice more early in the second half.

They appeared to be heading to a certain defeat only for Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu both to score in stoppage time.

Carrick, whose future has come under increasing scrutiny, repeatedly said United needed to 'tighten up' during his post-match interview with Sky Sports but didn't give much else away on his future.

"It's obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn't say much. I don't know if that's a tactic. Like a politician," Keane said afterwards on Sky.

"He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on. But they better get moving on that. It's the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren't very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it's just going to continue.

"What are we expecting to change over the next few weeks and months? What are they working on? They need to do a lot better than that."

Keane felt United deserved credit for fighting back to claim a point against Villa but lambasted their defending.

The former United midfielder added: "I think we've said previously there have been question marks over this team but they're showing a bit of fight, a bit of desire and, as bad as the game was from a footballing point of view, they kept going to the end.

"So, on the one hand, you say dreadful to give up four goals at home, but they kept going, so we have to give them a little bit of praise.

"In terms of the bigger picture, it's that rollercoaster of watching United. Some bits were so, so bad. Defensively the way it started, the start of the second half, but they found a way to get a point in a game where they looked dead and buried.

"Still nowhere near good enough to try and get towards the middle of the table."

United have dropped into the relegation zone and still boast only one Premier League victory to their name this season, and former defender Ashley Young was scathing in his assessment.

Young said: "There's got to be so much more communication going through this team. It looks like they don't even know each other at times. It's tough to watch.

"You're looking at the fans, they're probably wondering what they've just witnessed. Of course there's a lot of young players but there's got to be more leaders out there on the pitch."

articles.headline: What if Manchester United had hired Jurgen Klopp?
articles.description: If Manchester United hired an all-time great like Jurgen Klopp, would they have won the Premier League? Let's find out!
articles.headlineJa: もしマンチェスター・ユナイテッドがユルゲン・クロップを招聘していたら？
articles.descriptionJa: もしマンチェスター・ユナイテッドがユルゲン・クロップのような歴史的な名将を監督に迎えていたら、プレミアリーグで優勝できていたのだろうか？その答えを探ってみよう！
articles.body:
Right around this time every year, you can start to feel it. The air gets a little crisper. The shadows get a little colder. The days get shorter. The tree colors start to pop. You start wearing sweaters. Pumpkins appear in places where they do and do not belong.

Everyone and everything starts to shift, just slightly, in preparation for what's about to happen. The cycles of nature can be fickle and unpredictable, so the date is never exactly the same, and some years come and go without anything at all. But most years, it does.

Our tiny little rituals prime us to anticipate the inevitable, oncoming shift: that moment when Manchester United fire their manager and convince themselves that the new guy is finally going to be the one who fixes everything.

Ruben Amorim lost his job last January. Erik ten Hag was fired two years ago, right before Halloween. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer got the boot just a couple of days before Thanksgiving. And Jose Mourinho was relieved of his duties a little over a week before Christmas.

Now that we've once again entered the season of sacking, Michael Carrick seems like he will inevitably become the latest victim.

Man United are in the relegation zone. If history is any indication, their comeback against AS Roma in the Champions League will end up being meaningless. Before Tuesday's win, Carrick appeared to be on the verge of tears at the end of every match.

This is the 14th season since Manchester United last won the Premier League. And whoever replaces Carrick will be the ninth coach to try to do something that no other United manager since has done: just, simply, meet the expectations at one of the richest sports teams on the planet for more than a single season in a row.

But given how many different coaches have now failed since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club, it makes you wonder: Could anyone have been successful at Manchester United?

What is a great manager worth?

Arsenal won the Premier League last season with 85 points.

If we lived in a world where there were no subs and everyone on the field contributed exactly evenly to their team's success, then all 11 Arsenal players would have contributed about 8 points (7.7, to be slightly more exact) of value last season.

Except, the alternative to each player isn't just zero points. If you removed Bukayo Saka from the lineup, you wouldn't have to play a man down. No, you'd get to put another player out there who would also contribute to winning to some degree.

So, let's look at the relegation-level cutoff. West Ham were relegated with 39 points. Using the same framework, we'd say that all of their players were worth a little over 3.5 points across the season. We could then say that the average Arsenal player provided 5 more points of value than a relegation-level player.

articles.headline: Man United rescue 4-4 draw vs. Aston Villa but remain in relegation zone
articles.description: Manchester United fought back for a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday after twice going two goals down at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Manchester United fought back for a barely-believable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday after twice going two goals down at Old Trafford, but remain in the Premier League relegation zone.

Old Trafford witnessed an astonishing rollercoaster encounter as Michael Carrick's embattled, and deeply flawed, side showed spirit against the odds -- as they had against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday -- amid a backdrop of anger against the club's ownership.

Unai Emery's Villa looked set to pile the pressure on Carrick after going 2-0 up inside four minutes and 4-2 up after a similarly fast start to the second half, but United completed a remarkable comeback thanks to goals off the bench from Joshua Zirkzee and a 97th-minute leveler from Patrick Dorgu.

The result still means United go into the international break in 18th, and have won just one league game this season, back in August. Their eight-game winless league run means Carrick's position as boss may still not be safe despite the fightback.

United fell two goals behind -- in a club-record three minutes and 42 seconds -- as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson capitalised on wretched play. The mood that was already sour as supporters called for the Glazers and United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to sell up, only worsened.

Green and yellow balloons also filled the air, fans displayed a banner that read "we don't want a new stadium, we want new owners," while furious chants went up a notch.

But a poorly-timed challenge from Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha gifted United a penalty and captain Bruno Fernandes converted from the spot, just like in the 3-2 comeback win over Roma. Youri Tielemans then equalised against his former club just before halftime.

- As it happened: Man United 4-4 Aston Villa

- Man United's poor starts have PL relegation looking more likely

But renewed United hope was dented at the start of the second half, with John McGinn scoring a penalty gifted to Villa by Diogo Dalot -- whose substitution would be brutally cheered -- before Leon Goretzka added another.

They were the latest self-inflicted wounds in a season of gaffes by Carrick's side but the players fought until the death, with Zirkzee reducing the deficit in stoppage time before fellow substitute Dorgu sparked bedlam.

Dorgu rose to head home a Fernandes corner, with Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki's appeals he was upended trying to meet the cross ignored.

Under-fire Carrick left applauding fans chanting his name at the end of a crazy game.

Afterwards, Carrick told Sky: "We haven't won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working what we've been working on, tighten up on a few mistakes, and win football matches."

Information from ESPN Global Research and PA was used in this report.

Cleveland Cavaliers (5-5, seventh in the Eastern Conference) vs. Charlotte Hornets (3-7, 10th in the Eastern Conference)


              Charlotte, North Carolina; Monday, 7 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Charlotte looks to stop its six-game losing streak when the Hornets take on Cleveland.


              Charlotte finished 44-38 overall, 26-26 in Eastern Conference action and 21-20 at home during the 2025-26 season. The Hornets averaged 15.6 points off of turnovers, 17.9 second-chance points and 36.2 bench points last season.


              Cleveland went 52-30 overall and 33-19 in Eastern Conference action during the 2025-26 season. The Cavaliers gave up 115.4 points per game while committing 19.6 fouls last season.


              INJURIES: Hornets: Kon Knueppel: day to day (leg), Moussa Diabate: day to day (quadriceps), Dennis Schroder: day to day (soreness), Grant Williams: day to day (hamstring), Brandon Miller: day to day (groin).


              Cavaliers: Jarrett Allen: out (knee), Nae'Qwan Tomlin: out (back), Jaylon Tyson: out (ankle), Sam Merrill: out (elbow).
